rules.title: California tenant screening fee cap and itemization requirements
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge a screening fee only up to the annually adjusted state maximum and only for actual screening costs. They must give the applicant a receipt itemizing out-of-pocket costs and time spent, a copy of any credit report obtained, and a refund of any unused portion.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords or agents charging prospective residential tenants a fee to screen applications in California.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is

rules.title: No screening fee when no unit is available; refund to unselected applicants
rules.requirement: A landlord may not charge a screening fee if no rental unit is actually available. The landlord must return fees to applicants not selected, unless it reviews applications first-come-first-served and does not charge applicants who are not considered.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords charging screening fees to prospective residential tenants in California.
rules.exemptions: Landlords using a first-come-first-served policy who do not charge applicants who are not considered need not refund.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord cannot charge a prospective tenant a screening fee if no rental unit is actually available.
rules.conflict_note: The page states this as current law but does not tie it to a specific subsection or effective date.

rules.title: Required tenant screening fee rights statement
rules.requirement: An owner who charges an application or credit-report fee must give a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement before receiving the fee. The owner must also state the maximum fee permitted under Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b), either in the application or in a separate disclosure.
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners or agents of residential property in Berkeley who charge applicants a screening or application fee.

rules.title: Ban on non-refundable fees for existing tenancies
rules.requirement: Owners may not charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy. This includes fees tied to a roommate's departure or to adding or replacing a roommate. Under BMC 13.78.018, the rule applies regardless of contrary lease terms.
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental agreements in Berkeley, including existing leases.
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.
